slides.head:
Nearly 8 in 10 surveyed editors
use AI. Few want it to cut.
77.5% already use it.
slides.body: Avid surveyed 120 of the roughly 1,200 members of American Cinema Editors. 77.5% said they use AI somewhere in post-production.

slides.head: The busywork goes first.
slides.body: The top uses are transcription (60%), audio cleanup (55%) and searching hundreds of hours of footage for one shot (39.2%).

slides.head: Half a day, 15 minutes.
slides.body: On a recent season of MasterChef, editor Molly Shock says AI search found multiple examples of a shot within seconds. Some days, half a day's work dropped to 15 minutes.

slides.head: The cut stays human.
slides.body: Only 7.5% want AI to help assemble shots or rough cuts. Ethical, copyright and security concerns are nearly 50% of what holds editors back.

slides.head: Let AI log. You cut.
slides.body: Working editors hand AI the transcripts, the cleanup and the search, and keep every creative decision. That is the line worth holding in your own edit.
